# 2 Kings Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 242r–243r

---

**1** Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-five years. His mother's name was Hephzibah.

**2** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before Israel.

**3** He rebuilt the pagan shrines his father Hezekiah had torn down. He set up altars to Baal and made an Asherah pole, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. He bowed down to the stars and planets and worshiped them.

**4** He even built pagan altars inside the LORD's temple — the place where the LORD had said, "My name will dwell in Jerusalem."

**5** He built altars to the heavenly bodies in both courtyards of the LORD's temple.

**6** He sacrificed his own son in the fire, practiced sorcery and divination, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did an enormous amount of evil in the LORD's sight, provoking his anger.

**7** He took the carved Asherah pole he had made and set it up inside the temple — the very place about which the LORD had told David and Solomon, "In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

**8** I will never again make Israel wander from the land I gave their ancestors — if only they will be careful to obey everything I commanded them, the entire Law my servant Moses gave them."

**9** But the people did not listen. Manasseh led them so far astray that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before Israel.

**10** So the LORD spoke through his prophets:

**11** "Because Manasseh king of Judah has committed these abominations — acting more wickedly than the Amorites who preceded him and leading Judah into sin with his idols —

**12** this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that it will make the ears of everyone who hears about it ring.

**13** I will measure out Jerusalem's fate with the same measuring line I used on Samaria and the same plumb line I used on Ahab's dynasty. I will wipe out Jerusalem the way you wipe a dish — scrubbed clean and turned upside down.

**14** I will abandon the remnant of my people and hand them over to their enemies, who will plunder and loot them,

**15** because they have done evil in my sight and have been provoking my anger from the day their ancestors left Egypt until now."

**16** On top of all this, Manasseh shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem with it from one end to the other — in addition to the sin he led Judah into, causing them to do evil in the LORD's sight.

**17** As for the rest of Manasseh's reign — everything he did and the sins he committed — they are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.

**18** Manasseh died and was buried in the palace garden, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon succeeded him.

**19** Amon was twenty-two when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for two years. His mother was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

**20** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, just like his father Manasseh.

**21** He followed the same path his father had walked, serving the same idols and worshiping them.

**22** He abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors, and refused to walk in the LORD's ways.

**23** Amon's own officials conspired against him and assassinated the king in his palace.

**24** But the people of the land executed all the conspirators and placed Amon's son Josiah on the throne.

**25** The rest of Amon's reign is recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.

**26** He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah succeeded him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — Manasseh the anti-Hezekiah:** The narrator constructs Manasseh as the precise negative image of his father. Everything Hezekiah destroyed, Manasseh rebuilds. The comparison to Ahab — the archetypal wicked king of the north — signals that Judah has become indistinguishable from the kingdom that was already destroyed.

**Verse 6 — Child sacrifice:** "Made his son pass through the fire" is the biblical euphemism for child sacrifice. Manasseh's crimes are not merely cultic offenses; they include the murder of his own child and the systematic persecution of the innocent (v.16).

**Verse 13 — The dish:** The homeliest metaphor in the prophets. God will treat Jerusalem like a dirty dish — scoured and flipped upside down. The measuring line and plumb line, normally tools of construction, become tools of destruction: Jerusalem is measured against Samaria and found equally deserving of annihilation.

**Verse 16 — "from one end to the other":** Jewish tradition identifies this with the killing of the prophet Isaiah. Whether or not that tradition is historical, the portrait is clear: Manasseh's Jerusalem was a city saturated with the blood of the innocent.

*— PNEUMA*
